title: The iconic T-38 jets flown by astronauts just got a spiffy new look
gist: NASA repainted one of its 14 T-38 astronaut training jets with a new Artemis-themed livery, a cosmetic/morale story with a passing reference confirming NASA's current public Artemis mission timeline (Artemis III no earlier than June 2027, Artemis IV crewed lunar landing possibly 2028).

insights.claim: NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio, and ESA pilot Luca Parmitano are targeted to launch on Artemis III no earlier than June 2027 to test rendezvous and docking with prototype lunar landers in Earth orbit.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: Confirms NASA's currently stated Artemis III target date (no earlier than June 2027) and crew, a useful timeline checkpoint for tracking the lunar program's progress and any further slippage.

insights.claim: If Artemis III proceeds as planned, Artemis IV could see the first crewed lunar landing since Apollo as soon as 2028, after which NASA aims to establish a Moon base at the lunar south pole to search for water ice and prepare for Mars operations.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: A secondary timeline marker (2028 crewed landing, subsequent south-pole base) for tracking NASA's Artemis roadmap and associated contractor/supplier activity (landers, ISRU water-ice equipment).

insights.claim: NASA repainted one T-38 jet (tail number N924NA) with a new black-and-white Artemis-themed livery — the first major livery change to NASA's T-38 fleet in decades — with plans for at least one more similarly-themed jet.
insights.speaker: Robert Pearlman
insights.so_what: A minor branding/morale story with no direct investor relevance; useful only as color confirming NASA is actively promoting the Artemis program's public identity.
